editorial:
Gang Busters is a 13-chapter Universal serial from 1942, produced by Ford Beebe and directed by Noel M. Smith and Ray Taylor. It stars Kent Taylor as Det. Lt. Bill Bannister, with Irene Hervey, Ralph Morgan as the villain Professor Mortis, and Robert Armstrong. It opens with "The League of Murdered Men" and was adapted from the Gang Busters radio series, with Phillips Lord credited as a writer. Film Classics re-released it in 1949 (per Wikipedia). With a running time of about four hours (251 minutes across 13 chapters), the cliffhanger material and recognisable title suit compilation, commentary or clip work.

The rights question is open, not settled. A 1942 film needed a renewal around 1969-1970 to keep its copyright. Our check of the Catalog of Copyright Entries volumes was incomplete, and the Copyright Office online records (1978 onward) cannot settle a 1969-1970 renewal, so we have not confirmed that no renewal exists. Check the Catalog renewal sections yourself before relying on the print. Separately, the radio source and the GANG BUSTERS name may carry their own rights, and online copies may be VHS-sourced or colorized, which may add protected material.
faq: Is the 1942 Gang Busters serial free to reuse?

Not confirmed. The print's status depends on whether Universal renewed the copyright around 1969-1970. Our catalog check was incomplete. Search the 1969 and 1970 Catalog of Copyright Entries renewal sections (and the 1960-1969 cumulative) yourself. The Copyright Office online records cover only 1978 onward and cannot confirm a 1969-1970 renewal, so ask the Copyright Office directly if the catalogs leave doubt.
Does the Gang Busters name or radio source create extra risk?

Possibly. The serial was based on the Gang Busters radio series, and we did not research that source's copyright or any current trademark on the title. Check both before using the name commercially, even if the film itself is clear.
